definition: The documented history and origin of a dataset, including where it came from, how it was collected, and any transformations applied to it.
details: Data provenance is important for assessing dataset quality, licensing compliance, and potential biases, and has become a more prominent concern as training datasets for LLMs have grown to enormous, often loosely documented scale.
story: Picture a librarian organizing a million slips of paper so that any one of them can be found in a heartbeat. The examples a machine reads become the world it believes in. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Garbage in, garbage out — and the reverse: clean, representative data makes the model quietly brilliant. And that is Data Provenance — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
